slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Sole image at EEPROM block 0; FUN_080ce3cc (0x080ce3cc) reads 0x1A8 bytes via FUN_080e7654, validates complement-sum8 at byte 0x00 over 0x01..0x1A7; on read failure or checksum mismatch it installs RAM defaults and clears *_DAT_080ce560, on match it sets *puRam080ce574=1. No backup copy, mirroring, or generation counter exists in the 512-byte image; bytes 0x1A8..0x1FF are unused 0xFF.

checksums.name: eeprom_image_sum8_complement
checksums.formula_detail: stored byte[0x00] == (~(sum of bytes[0x01..0x1A7] mod 256)) & 0xFF; ones-complement of an 8-bit additive sum, seed 0, no XOR/CRC. Decompiled validator: FUN_080ce3cc adds each byte from buffer+1 into byte accumulator bVar2 and tests (byte)*_DAT_080ce548 == (byte)~bVar2; loop bound _DAT_080ce544 is DAT-unresolved, covered end 0x1A7 pinned by loader length 0x1A8 (FUN_080e7654 call in FUN_080ce3cc) plus byte verification.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive (FUN_080e8408): writes src/dst/count|0x80000000 to DAT-unresolved registers matching DMA3SAD/DAD/CNT at 0x040000D4..0x040000DC by pattern, spins on busy bit 0x8000. Used for both EEPROM command and data phases; role at this level is bus transfer, direction set by caller.

EEPROM 8-byte block read (sole MMIO seed): builds start+read-opcode+address bitstream on stack, DMAs address_bits+3 halfwords to 0x0D000000, DMAs 0x44 halfwords back, repacks 64 bits into dest[0..7] in reverse halfword order. Caller edge is textual (func_0x080e8488 at decompiled.c line 8042); callgraph.json lists no callers. No EEPROM write/program counterpart exists in the corpus.

Sequential EEPROM reader: loops FUN_080e8488 over consecutive blocks (RAM block counter via _DAT_080e7670, dest += 8, length -= 8), returns 1 on completion / 0 on failure. Called with length 0x1A8 at decompiled.c line 292.

Load/validate/default-initialise entry (no caller in corpus): calls FUN_080e7290, FUN_080e7654(save_buffer,0x1A8); on read failure or checksum mismatch installs defaults (offsets in report Section 3.5) and calls FUN_080ce710/FUN_080ce8d0; on match sets valid flag. Also the checksum routine for this format.

Deserialiser into working RAM: 16 records x 8B from src+0x0C (0xFF sentinel -> -1 else <<11), verbatim bulk copies of 9/180/40/40 bytes between DAT-unresolved pointers, header bit-fields from src[7..11], trailer u16@0x19A/0x19C and u32@0x1A0/0x1A4 (swapped). Caller textual from FUN_080ce3cc branches.
Bit-field unpacker for packed header bytes 0x00..0x05 into a separate RAM struct. Caller textual from FUN_080ce3cc.

BIOS CpuSet SWI 0x0B wrapper (FUN_080e8380), used by FUN_080ce3cc to copy default blocks into the RAM save buffer. Not an EEPROM writer; included because it is the only copy primitive on the default path. Role label serialize is approximate: RAM-to-RAM copy only.

open_questions: No EEPROM write/program driver exists among the 221 traced functions: every .sav writer attribution, the save trigger, and any per-save generation counter are unattributed. The writer must be located in untraced ROM code (packet cold-reload probe proves saves persist at runtime).

sav-00-f1723.sav fails the verified checksum (stored 0x00, computed 0xBD) because bytes 0xB8..0x1A7 are still 0xFF: incomplete/intermediate capture versus an image the boot validator would reject is undecided (fuzz test F9).

All RAM mirror addresses are unknown: relevant pointers are unresolved _DAT_080xxxxx literal-pool symbols (_DAT_080ce474, _DAT_080e7670, _DAT_080e8534, etc.) whose values are not in the corpus, so fields are located only relative to the save-buffer base.
Checksum loop bound _DAT_080ce544 is DAT-unresolved; covered end 0x1A7 is inferred from loader length 0x1A8 plus verification on sav-01 (and failure on sav-00), not read as a literal.
Initial value of the EEPROM block counter (_DAT_080e7670 target) is not in the corpus; block 0 start is inferred from the checksum covering file byte 0x00.

Default-init writes in FUN_080ce3cc do not byte-match the observed .sav header (e.g. byte 0x01 observed 0x20 vs default mask|0x01): an absent serialiser/bit-packer transform, or a working-struct base that is not byte-identical to the EEPROM image, must intervene.

AMOT (0x88) and IIAA (0x94) are byte-verified ASCII but never compared in code; AMOT also conflicts with the record-15 +4 byte under the FUN_080ce8d0 record stride. Name/signature versus record data is undecided (fuzz tests F5/F6).
Semantics of the 16 records at 0x0C (what an entry represents), header bytes 0x01..0x0B, regions 0x98..0x199, and trailer fields 0x19A..0x1A7 are code-located but game-meaning unknown.
Offsets of FUN_080ce8d0 verbatim bulk copies (9, 180, 40, 40 bytes) within the save image are unrecoverable from DAT-unresolved pointers; the UNKNOWN regions 0x98..0x199 are only candidates.

FUN_080ce3cc has no caller in the corpus and its checksum-success branch does not call the unpackers in the traced code; the boot entry point and any post-validation unpack step are outside the traced functions.

EEPROM block-count limit *(ushort *)(_DAT_080e84a0+4) and address-bit count byte *_DAT_080e8534+8 are DAT-unresolved; 53-block usage is proven by the loader call, total device geometry (64 blocks) by file size.
